binary.rule: if structuredContent is present (and the call is not an error): the model gets JSON.stringify(structuredContent) as one text block; the content array's text blocks are dropped; its non-text blocks (image, audio, resource) are kept, in front of the JSON. Without structuredContent the content array is passed as is. An isError result never carries structuredContent to the model.
binary.gate: a remote feature flag (`tengu_eventual_noodle`, default false, telemetry event `mcp_content_over_structured`) flips the rule: content first, structuredContent only when every content text is blank. Off in both measured versions for this account.
binary.size_guard: structuredContent over 1,048,576 chars of JSON (8,388,608 for a tool with a ui:// resource) is left off the result message; content is then kept

live_session_probe: eval-best render_table (2.1.308): the result was the echoed structuredContent {columns, data, title, queryIntent}; the content text {interpretation: {alerts}, rendered} did not arrive. The same tool's refusal (isError, no structuredContent) arrived as text.

retroactive.method: result_chars (the length of the tool_result block in each subagent transcript, extract.py) against the serialized input, for every successful render call in the eval results
retroactive.finding: every render_chart / render_table / render_map result in Q22, Q22b, Q22c, Q23, Q24 (pilot and confirm) is the input plus 10–400 chars of normalisation: the structuredContent echo. `best`'s content text with interpretation.alerts, and `best-v1`'s one-line confirmation, never reached the model.
retroactive.consequence: Q22b measured an alert that was not delivered. Its reading 'an alert after a successful render is read as a note' is withdrawn; 2/10 headers fixed and 0/10 re-renders are what an absent alert scores. Q22c stands, and now has its mechanism: a refusal is an error result, and an error result delivers its content text. Every chart alert of `best` (pie slices, line series, radar) was likewise undelivered on Claude Code; results that counted only the chart type chosen are unaffected.

headline: Each host reads a different channel. Claude Code: structuredContent only, whenever present. claude.ai chat: content only, structuredContent only when content is empty. ChatGPT Chat: both without an outputSchema, structuredContent only with one. No host delivered _meta. Every host delivered an error result's content text.

So the only portable form is a mirror: the same meaning in structuredContent and in the content text. A tool that puts meaning in only one channel loses it on at least one host: content-only meaning on Claude Code and on ChatGPT with an outputSchema, structuredContent-only meaning on claude.ai.

Q22b's alert sat in content beside a structuredContent echo, so on Claude Code (where every eval ran) it never arrived; its conclusion is withdrawn. On claude.ai the same tool would have delivered the alert and not the payload.
Q22c stands: a refusal is an error result, and every host delivered its text.
caveats: The behaviour sits behind a remote flag; another account or a later rollout can flip it. Re-probe before relying on it.
Probe on haiku, n=1 per tool per version; the conversion is deterministic code, so n measures nothing here.
Chat-host results are self-reports (two runs each), checked against unique fingerprints, as in HD; the Claude Code result is read from the delivered tool_result.
claude.ai: the connector was added as a team connector (the only option offered) and removed after the runs. Cowork, ChatGPT Work and Codex not run.
fix: Same day, in source: best's render_chart, render_table and render_map return interpretation and rendered first in structuredContent, before the UI payload, with the same JSON as the content text (src/tools/app-tools-best.ts bestRenderResult; tests in app-tools-best.test.ts). Not deployed to mcpBest at the time of writing; not re-measured.
